newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH GOVT "POSITIVE" ABOUT PACCAR BID FOR DAF.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH GOVT "POSITIVE" ABOUT PACCAR BID FOR DAF.

text.p: The Dutch ministry of economic affairs said on Monday news U.S. truck-maker Paccar Inc planned a bid worth 933 million guilders for DAF Trucks NV appeared on first examination to be positive.

The Dutch government holds a 39 percent stake in DAF Trucks, the result of a rescue operation which followed the 1993 bankruptcy of DAF Trucks' predecessor, DAF NV. Another 10 percent is held by the government of the Belgian region of Flanders and the rest by banks and institutional investors.
"The minister's first response to this bid is positive but it will be a few weeks before a decision," said a spokesman.

The spokesman said economics affairs minister Hans Wijers was likely to seek a "fairness opinion" from a group of financial advisors who would go over the Paccar bid and give their opinion of the merits of the offer.
Wijers would also take into account industrial and political factors when making his decision about the Dutch state's stake.

"Price will be important of course, but he will weigh up the bid from the point of industrial policy -- that there will still be a truck company in the Netherlands which is embedded in our industrial and technical structure," said the spokesman. -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
